label: early input of a new x/f/0/e/r/n (steps 2-6)
explanation: Fires only in the original-input phase (92% of mass) and at the delimiter (8%); never during copy. Confined to t=2..6, peaking at t=3; nothing at t=0-1 or t>=8. Within that window it prefers the first occurrence of an input token (91% of mass), especially x, f, 0 (about 4x lift each), then e, r, n; z, o, h and <DEL> give weaker firing. Magnitude goes up when the sequence starts with v, u, d, k, s, b, 2 or w: adding that condition raises precision to 0.87 but cuts recall to 0.23. All steps t=2..6 in the original/delimiter phase cover 99% of mass at precision 0.14, so the window is clean but the token/history dependence is graded and spread across many tokens. The predicate gets about 0.55 F1 / 0.67 mass recall on dev.
